clue.text: Founder shows pointless to wake up around cross, pointless

indicators.note: around tells us the first trimmed word wraps itself about the second
pointless means losing a compass point, here the E at the end

parts.note: to rouse someone is to wake them up

indicators.note: pointless again strips a compass point, the final E of the hybrid animal

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a founder for being lazy and cross, apparently getting nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'pointless' trims take off an E (East, a compass point): ROUS goes 'around' MUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Romulus is the legendary founder of Rome, so he is the founder by tradition.

clue.text: See 15
Untidy person to spoil company game in Donn Byrne's book

parts.note: one who makes a mess is a messer
to mar something is to spoil it
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: A slob ruins a firm's sporting outing, as told in a novel by Donn Byrne.
explanation.definitionFit: Messer Marco Polo is a 1921 novel by the Irish-American writer Donn Byrne, so it names that book.

clue.text: Run in a floppy sort of way to remove first page from sweet

definitions.text: Run in a floppy sort of way

indicators.note: to remove means those letters are taken out of the sweet

parts.note: a lollipop is a sweet on a stick
I, the Roman numeral one, stands for first

explanation.surface: Instructions on running lazily, followed by tearing a page out of a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first page' is I (one) plus P; taking that pair out of LOLLIPOP leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To lollop is to move with an ungainly bounding or floppy gait, like a loping dog.

clue.text: Pub in heaven, not for stout?

indicators.note: in tells us the pub sits inside the heavens

parts.note: the sky stands for the heavens
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A pub in paradise that refuses to serve a dark beer such as Guinness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like the beer, but here it means fat: a skinny person is the opposite of stout.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinny describes someone thin, which is the reverse of stout in its sense of plump.

clue.text: Meat for tea? Leave with none, say?

parts.note: char is a British slang word for tea

indicators.note: with none, say tells us the leaving word goes without any of the tea just mentioned, its letter T

parts.note: to quit is to leave

explanation.surface: A question whether meat counts as the evening meal, and whether you should walk out with nothing to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with none, say' means QUIT goes without T, sounding like the 'tea' already mentioned, which leaves QUI.
explanation.definitionFit: Charqui is South American dried beef, the original of jerky, so it is a kind of meat.

clue.text: Test place for Benaud, say, evokes free style compositions

parts.note: a cap is awarded for a place in a Test team

indicators.note: say tells us a word spoken is entered by its sound

parts.note: Richie Benaud was the Australian Test cricket captain and commentator

explanation.surface: A Test selection for the Australian cricketer conjures up loosely structured pieces of music.
explanation.walkthrough: Test is a Test match in cricket, and a cap marks selection; RICCI sounds like Richie, Benaud's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricci are lively musical pieces in a free form, plural of capriccio.

clue.text: One way of expressing distaste

parts.note: one is the article a
a version is one way of putting or rendering something

explanation.surface: A remark that one way to show displeasure is simply to say so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One way of expressing' reads like a description of the definition, but it is A VERSION.
explanation.definitionFit: Aversion is a strong dislike or disinclination, a synonym of distaste.

clue.text: Coloratura role for the moon

definitions.meaning: the star soprano part in Mozart's opera The Magic Flute, famed for high runs
a poetic title for the moon, which reigns over the dark hours

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a famous Mozart soprano part and a poetic name for the moon.

clue.text: Flint, he and she, may be actually there

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters can be made into something else

explanation.surface: Fred and Wilma style: Flint, he and she, could turn up in person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' turns FLINTHESHE into the phrase; 'and' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being present in the flesh means being physically there in person.

clue.text: Leisure — and it's starting to be used for painting

annotationWithheld.why: Leisure — and it's starting to be used for painting — EASE (Leisure) + L, but L is the start of 'Leisure' itself, so 'Leisure' does two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Leisure — and it's starting to be used for painting

clue.text: Put into effect by ordinary blokes beheaded before time

indicators.note: beheaded tells us the phrase loses its first letter

parts.note: simple means plain or ordinary
men are blokes

explanation.surface: Something enacted by common men who were executed before their time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' removes the S at the front of SIMPLE MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To implement a plan is to carry it out or put it into effect.

clue.text: Rise of the modern world includes study in scouting

indicators.note: includes tells us the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: the Renaissance marked the birth of the modern world in European history
to con is an old word for study or learn

explanation.surface: A history lecture on how modern life began, with a module on scouting.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconnaissance is military scouting to gather information about an area or enemy.

clue.text: Control for the majority when deserter's about

indicators.note: about says the letters move around into a new order

parts.note: the most is the majority
a rat is one who deserts a cause

explanation.surface: A ruling for most people when a turncoat is on the loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserter's' is 'deserter is'; 'about' rearranges THEMOST and RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermostat is a device that regulates or controls temperature.

clue.text: Most of pouffe on the back

indicators.note: most of tells us the exclamation loses its final letter

parts.note: pouf or pouffe is an exclamation of scorn, like humph

explanation.surface: Sitting on a footstool behind someone for most of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pouffe' looks like a footstool but is used as a snort of contempt, the same as HUMPH.
explanation.definitionFit: A hump is a rounded lump found on the back, as on a camel.

clue.text: Opus 150 of composer: how much ice cream can he have?

definitions.text: how much ice cream can he have?

indicators.note: a composer puts things together, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A catalogue number of a composer's work, followed by a question about his dessert ration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composer' looks like a musician, but signals that OPUS, CL and OF are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoopful is the measure of ice cream served at one go.

clue.text: Reduces sail area: it's a keen fear causes this

indicators.note: causes this says the letters before it produce the answer when rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor admits a sharp fear is behind shortening sail.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'it's' is ignored, giving ITS among the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking in a reef is the nautical manoeuvre of reducing the sail area in strong wind.

clue.text: Invite ten good turns for one nice little piece

annotationWithheld.why: Invite ten good turns for one nice little piece — the parse is an anagram of TEN G put inside VITE, with 'Invite' read as 'in VITE'; that splits one clue word into an indicator and a leaf, which a leaf cannot hold
annotationWithheld.clue: Invite ten good turns for one nice little piece

clue.text: Artists' warning of French twitcher's trophy?

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist; two of them give RA twice
avis is French for a notice or warning

explanation.surface: Painters receive a caution from France about a birdwatcher's prize.
explanation.walkthrough: A twitcher is a keen birdwatcher, whose prize sighting is a rare bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Rara avis is Latin for rare bird, the prize a birdwatcher hopes to spot.

clue.text: Time for Protestant to use incense?

parts.note: Jan Hus was a Czech reformer, a forerunner of Protestantism

explanation.surface: A question of whether it is time for a Protestant to burn incense in church.
explanation.walkthrough: Thus is an old word for frankincense; Protestant churches traditionally shun incense, hence the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus is a gum resin, frankincense, burnt as an aromatic offering.

clue.text: International spring is sick

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, stands for international
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: A news line that a worldwide water source is polluted.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwell means ill or sick, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Wood-eating insect giving brilliant display

indicators.note: eating tells us the insect takes the wood inside itself

parts.note: a fly is an insect
ash is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: A woodworm-like bug putting on a dazzling show.
explanation.definitionFit: Flashy means showy or ostentatiously bright, putting on a glittering display.

clue.text: April wish — throw bone at dog with Lenin

indicators.note: throw means the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A springtime wish to hurl a bone at a dog alongside the Soviet leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link, not fodder. The answer opens Browning's poem Home-Thoughts, from Abroad, written in April.
explanation.definitionFit: Browning wished to be in England now that April was there, so the phrase is that April wish.

clue.text: Unbound from 1 down

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are drawn out of the other entry and remade

parts.note: the solution to 1 down, a band of sail rolled up

explanation.surface: Released from the clue above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Free means not tied or confined, a synonym of unbound.

clue.text: Let it off between 10s at point that's no use at all

indicators.note: between means the jumble sits within the pair of tools

parts.note: 10 across is an implement, and an implement is a tool
a second tool from the same plural

indicators.note: off says the two words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
E, East, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Advice to release someone at a certain point, too late to matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 across is IMPLEMENT, so '10s' are tools, giving both TOOLs from one word. E is East, a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Something offered in insufficient quantity and too tardily is of no use at all.

clue.text: Term of endearment sets back newspaper (American)

indicators.note: sets back means the pieces are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a rag is a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: A pet name for someone is a blow to an American tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar is used as an affectionate name for a loved one, like honey.

clue.text: See 23
Much of the above keeping still for baby

indicators.note: keeping tells us the trimmed entry holds the other word inside
much of tells us part of that entry is dropped

parts.note: the entry just above, 25 across
yet means still

explanation.surface: Most of what was said earlier stays calm for an infant.
explanation.walkthrough: From TOO LATE above, 'Much of' keeps LATE, which holds YET.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is a set of clothes and linen for a newborn baby, so the word is used for baby gear.
